title: Several picked clips move onto another track together
goal: An editor who picks two or three clips and drags them up a track, to lay b-roll over the talk or move a group onto its own row, expects them all to go. Today a drag of several picked clips only slides them along in time; dragging one clip onto another track works, several does not, and nothing on screen says why.
notes: Sources/Photonz/EditorState+ClipBar.swift ~510: `case .body where !session.along.isEmpty` clears clipTrackDrop and only calls moveClips(byMS:). The single-clip path uses landClip(_:atInMS:moved:on:) with the ClipTrackDrop from the drag (EditorState+Tracks.swift ~336, 389). Needs a core move that shifts several layers by a track delta (PhotonzCore, test first: track index offset per clip, kinds checked, locked tracks refused). Premiere and Final Cut both move a multi-selection across tracks. Found by the 2026-10-05 22:xx manager pass reading the drag code, not on screen, hence the reproduce step.
acceptance: Reproduce first: pick two clips on V1 (Command click), drag one of them up onto V2 or the space above the top track, and write in the log what happens today

Several picked clips dragged up or down move together by the same number of tracks and the same time, as one undo step; a new track is made over the top when the drag goes above it, the way a single clip's drop does

A clip whose target track is locked, or the wrong kind (picture onto an audio track), stops the whole move from changing track and the drop shows the same not-allowed cue a single clip shows; the clips still slide in time
Each clip's linked sound stays linked and follows its picture

Try it at Next defaults: open a recording, Add Media at Playhead for a second clip, cut both, Command click two pieces, drag them up a track. A walk does the same and reads which track each clip landed on. Audit written under queue/audits/; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: Reproduced 2026-10-05 in the probe (walk Scripts/playtest/zz-repro-multi-track-walk.json, throwaway): recording trimmed to 6s on V1, b-roll dropped on V1 at 6s, both picked (dragClip click, then shift-click), clipCarryToNewTrackOnTopHeld + clipDragRelease. Result: 'expectClip FAILED: no clip called "Tutorial Sample" is on V2; the timeline: b-roll on V1 6.00s to 14.00s; Tutorial Sample on V1 0.00s to 6.00s'. Both stay on V1. Two causes in code: updateClipTrackDrop refuses any drop while session.along is non-empty (so a real drag shows no target), and commitClipBarDrag's .body-with-along branch clears clipTrackDrop and only slides in time.

Adversarial pass: Premiere moves a multi-selection by the same number of tracks (V clips up, A clips down mirrored); acceptance asks a positional shift with wrong kind refusing the whole track change, so a mixed picture + pure-sound pick moving up is refused (the sound would land on a picture track) and still slides in time. Linked sound is part of the picture layer (soundTrackID), so it stays on its audio track and follows in time with no extra work. Option-copy of several picked clips stays time-only for now (copies path not touched). A drop between two tracks with several clips: one new track at that place for the hand's track, every other clip shifted by the same rows, and rows above the top or below the bottom get new tracks made, as the single drop does.

Built: PhotonzCore ClipsAcrossTracks.swift (canMoveClips / moveClips(_:carrying:to:byMS:)), 13 tests in ClipsAcrossTracksTests; EditorState+Tracks updateClipTrackDrop now aims several moved clips (not ⌥ copies), setClipTrackDrop asks canMoveClips, landClips lands them in one perform; commitClipBarDrag's several-clips branch lands the track move when allowed, otherwise slides in time as before. Walk step dragClip gained tracksUp (pointer Y through updateClipTrackDrop from the dock's drawn rows) and ⌘ on a click extends the pick like ⇧.
